finding.claim: The /checkout handler computes the charge total from client-supplied price and qty. An authenticated user can set price to 0.01, or use a negative price or qty, to pay almost nothing or cause a negative charge (a refund-like credit). The server-side catalog is never consulted. The sibling /checkout-v2 handler looks up prices from req.catalog and clamps qty, so this route is the unprotected one.

trace.note: total = sum of i.price * i.qty, with both values taken from the request body
charge is called with the attacker-derived total
the total is echoed back with no validation

finding.guards_checked: No price lookup, no qty or price validation, no positive or finite check on total. Auth is not visible in this file; req.user is assumed to be set by upstream middleware, which was not present to read. Compared with /checkout-v2 (cart.js:10-18), which uses req.catalog.price and Math.max(1, Math.floor(qty)). I did not report v2's NaN or Infinity qty edge case as a finding.

verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no catalog lookup or validation, and cart.js:6 charges that total for req.user.id, while /checkout-v2 at cart.js:13-14 uses req.catalog.price and clamps qty. Auth middleware is not in the repo, but any authenticated user can reach the route.
